validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE cleared. P5101 is a specific, distinct FERC-certificated project -- the Kalama Lateral Project, docket CP15-8 (Northwest Pipeline LLC, a Williams subsidiary) -- not the Northwest Pipeline system as a whole and not a duplicate of any sibling row. Confirmed via a full FERC docket paper trail found through the Federal Register API (FERC's own eLibrary and oilandgaswatch.org are JS SPAs that could not be scraped; see notes on individual fills): pre-filing scoping (FR 2012-15837, Jun 2012), Section 7(c) application filed Oct 27 2014 naming 'Kalama Lateral Project' (FR 2014-26505), EA notices (FR 2014-29872, FR 2015-00735, FR 2015-17789), certificate authorized April 11 2016 (restated in FR 2020-06816), three construction-deadline extensions (2018, 2019, and a contested request in 2020 for a 2022 deadline -- FR 2020-06816), the docket listed on FERC's Oct 21 2021 Sunshine Act open-meeting agenda as item C-4 (FR 2021-22843), and EIA's own release history flipping the project's status from 'Approved/On Hold' (through the 2021-10 release) to 'Cancelled' (from the 2022-01 release onward, persisting through Aug2026 with the note 'Extended by FERC in 2019, but legal battles remain and construction has not started'). Roster check against the other four 'Northwest Gas Pipeline' rows in this batch (P0230 system row Sumas->Colorado 3,900 mi; P2626 Trail West/N-MAX Madras OR; P7790 Kelso-Beaver WA; P7812 Wild Trail UT) found no physical or docket overlap with Kalama (Cowlitz County WA short lateral to a proposed methanol plant at the Port of Kalama) -- distinct project, no cross_row duplicate. Caveat only: the original FERC application notice states 'approximately 3.1 miles' of pipeline vs. the sheet's recorded 3.00 mi; EIA's own workbook (all releases) independently states 3.0 mi exactly, matching the sheet -- an immaterial ~0.1 mi rounding difference between the applicant's approximate figure and the certificated/EIA figure, not staged as a spec concern. wiki_citations.json for this row was read in full (9 citations, all opened/tested): the co.williams.com and williams.com pages support Owner/Operator only (system-level, not Kalama-specific); the EIA data.php citation is a navigation page (never citable per standing rules) and was replaced throughout with dated EIA releases; the S&P Global 'gets 2 more years' article (previously cited on 4 units) is a real 403 bot-wall (confirmed by curl with a browser UA and by Wayback -- no snapshot exists for that URL, checked twice with a retry after a 429) and was replaced with primary FERC/Federal Register sources rather than deleted; oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/3307 (the current Location ref) returns HTTP 200 but is a bare Vue SPA shell with no server-rendered content -- reproduced via both WebFetch and curl, and via url_verifier which confirms 200-but-missing-expected-content -- and was replaced with the FERC application notice's location statement; the Sightline Institute and Bark Out wiki citations concern other Northwest Pipeline family projects (PNW gas buildout generally, and Trail West/P2626 respectively) and were not used for P5101. The routes-repo geojson for P5101 exists but carries a null geometry (one Feature, no coordinates) -- no route to sanity-check against. Orchestrator note: proposed_refs were empty on this record while it claimed tier=high / independent=true. A validity record carries no verifications by repo convention, so its tier is counted over proposed_refs -- an empty list reads as zero publishers and contradicts the claimed tier. Staged the two distinct publishers the prose already relies on for existence: the Federal Register notice of application naming the 'Kalama Lateral Project' under docket CP15-8, and EIA's dated Aug2026 pipeline-projects release which carries the project. The several other Federal Register notices cited in the prose are the same origin and are deliberately not listed as separate publishers.

The project was cancelled (per EIA, effective by the 2022-01 release) before ever breaking ground, consistent with three consecutive deadline extensions driven by permitting delays at the downstream methanol plant the lateral was built to serve, not by pipeline construction itself. Leaving ConstructionYear blank is the correct, sourced outcome, not an unresearched gap.
